I've been farming this land for 30 years. I know Quzhou's soil and weather. My father farmed here too. I do what works — what my neighbors do, what the village extension station says, what I've seen with my own eyes.

My 6 mu runs wheat and maize on the same 4 mu, rotating each year like always — wheat in winter, maize in summer. The other 2 mu I keep for stevia. Stevia brings in cash money, which the wheat and maize don't always do anymore.

**Wheat:** I'll buy improved certified seed from the county seed station, same variety I've used the last few years — yields are steady. I plow it rotary after the maize comes off in October, then plant. I water three times: the freeze water before winter sets in, then at jointing in March, then at heading. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and urea when it starts jointing. Three pesticide passes — herbicide in winter, then one spray in spring for disease and one for aphids if they show up.

**Maize:** I use hybrid seed, that's been the standard for 20 years now. I plant directly into the wheat stubble with no extra tillage — saves time and we always rush at wheat harvest. Summer rains help, so I only irrigate twice — at planting if the soil is dry, and at tasseling. Two pesticide rounds: herbicide early, then check for corn borer.

**Stevia:** This is the cash crop. I've had it 2 mu for a few years. I use divisions from my own plants — no need to buy. I prepare the soil in spring with rotary tillage, fertilize lighter than the grains since stevia doesn't need as much nitrogen. I water four times through the season and harvest leaves twice in summer-autumn. I dry and sell to the purchasing station.
